transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I have this intense, overwhelming fear of elevators and enclosed spaces that has been going on for about a year and a half now. It has gotten to the point where it's severely impacting my daily life and my job. I just don't know what to do anymore.
Did this fear of elevators and enclosed spaces start following a specific distressing or life-threatening event, such as being trapped or having a bad experience in one?
No, I don't recall any specific traumatic event, like getting trapped, that triggered this. It just seems to have developed and gotten worse over time.

Do you find that you experience this same level of intense, uncontrollable worry about many other different areas of your life, such as your health, finances, or work performance, even when you aren't near an elevator?

No, I don't worry like this about other areas of my life at all. My intense anxiety is strictly limited to elevators and being in enclosed spaces. Outside of those situations, I don't have that kind of overwhelming worry about my health, finances, or work.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denies the generalized, multi-domain worry characteristic of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Given that the anxiety is strictly limited to elevators and enclosed spaces (situational phobia), the diagnosis of Specific Phobia is much more strongly supported, and Generalized Anxiety Disorder can be ruled out.
